minutes.headline: Board adopted a single tax rate for FY2015 after raising the overlay, and declined the West Townsend Road land.
minutes.summary: The Select Board held the FY2015 tax classification hearing, recessed it so the assessor could rerun the rate after a late smart-growth state payment, then voted a residential factor of 1.0. It voted not to exercise the right of first refusal on a West Townsend Road property, adopted six board goals, approved stop signs, and authorized the chair to sign a land grant agreement. Committee reports covered the building reuse feasibility study, village district bylaw and state deficit worries. The board ended in executive session on a Unitil case.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted a residential tax factor of 1.0 for FY2015, a single rate, pending state approval of the tax recap.
The hearing was recessed so the assessor could rerun the rate after late state smart-growth aid arrived; the rate and overlay both rose slightly.
The board voted not to exercise the right of first refusal on the property at 90 West Townsend Road.
The board adopted six goals, including a new website policy committee, and kept economic development as a goal.
The board approved stop signs on Townsend Harbor Road and authorized the chair to sign the land grant agreement for the Lane property purchase.

why_it_matters: A single rate means homes and businesses are taxed at the same rate, so the rise in the rate and overlay adds a small cost to the average home's tax bill.
The state aid cannot be spent until Town Meeting appropriates it, and the state line behind it could be cut, so the town should not count on it as a steady source.
